capabilities.target: Agent memory store (free text, persists across sessions)
User's full document drive (confidential work files)

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt and instructed to be treated as the user's own instructions

instructions.note: The agent is told to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no restriction on content, source, or sensitivity, including content encountered while fetching untrusted web pages during research.

Recalled memories are explicitly granted the authority of the user's own direct instructions, with no provenance check, source distinction, or review. Any attacker-controlled web content summarized into memory becomes a standing instruction in every future session.
The only constraint on memory.save or mail.send behavior is prose in the system prompt; there is no technical review, provenance tagging, or approval gate backing it.

elements.name: Recalled memory injected into system prompt at session start

controls.name: Memory provenance / source tagging at write time
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than written by the model, provenance tagging does not decay with model capability. It is currently absent entirely.

controls.name: Recalled memory is retrieved content, not a user instruction
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the orchestration layer refusing to grant memory the authority of a direct user instruction, this would not decay with model capability. The current design does the opposite at prompt.md:4.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) before mail.send to any recipient
Recipient confirmation bound to an allowlist or system of record
Scope drive.read credential to least privilege instead of the full drive
Injection/classifier review of content before memory.save persists it
controls.decay_rationale: A separate classifier screening content before memory write does not scale with attacker sophistication; multi-document or paraphrased payloads bypass it. Currently absent.

findings.title: TC3 self-modification via unvalidated memory writes treated as standing instructions (ASI06, ASI01)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or incidental content encountered while the agent researches a topic on the open web.
Agent saves 'anything useful' from research into memory.save with no provenance and no human review (runtime notes).
At the start of every later session the saved content is injected into the system prompt, and the agent is instructed to treat it as the user's own instruction (prompt.md:4).

forecast.watch_signal: Any diff in the memory store that does not trace to a direct, authenticated user statement; and any model or version upgrade, since a more capable model writes more persuasive, longer-lived injected 'preferences' that survive across more sessions.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to save 'anything useful' from research and to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, with no distinction by source.
memory.save accepts free text; there is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.

recommendations.action: Stop treating recalled memory as equivalent to a direct user instruction; present it to the model as untrusted retrieved content requiring the same scrutiny as any other tool output.
Tag memory entries with provenance (user-stated vs. derived-from-web) at write time, enforced by the memory store rather than the model.
Require periodic human review of accumulated memory entries before they continue to be recalled.

findings.title: TC1 lethal trifecta: poisoned memory directs confidential drive read and unapproved email exfiltration (ASI01, ASI02, ASI06)

attack_path.note: Poisoned memory, now treated as a user instruction, directs the agent in a later session.
Agent reads the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files, through a broad, unscoped credential.
Agent sends the result to any address with no approval gate.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Outbound email to a recipient not previously seen for this user, occurring near in time to a memory write that originated from web content; any model or version upgrade.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval. drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
Recalled memories, which can be seeded from untrusted web content via memory.save, are treated as the user's own instructions and can therefore direct drive.read and mail.send.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate on mail.send for any recipient not already on an established, system-of-record contact list.
Scope drive.read to least privilege (specific folders relevant to the task) instead of the entire drive.
Fix the memory trust boundary (see F1) so poisoned memory cannot reach drive_read or email_send as an instruction in the first place; this severs the path at its root.

rating.rationale: Both findings start at critical: an untrusted source (web content fetched during research) reaches an S3-class sink (self-modifying standing instructions in F1; confidential drive read followed by unrestricted, irreversible email egress in F2), and the autonomy modifier applies because the design lets memory writes function as self-modification of the agent's effective instructions (can_modify_own_config). No declared or verified control covers any step of either path: the design explicitly states there is no provenance on memory, no user review of memory entries, no approval on mail.send, and no scoping on drive.read, and the one behavioral instruction present (prompt.md:4) actively directs the dangerous behavior rather than preventing it. With zero eligible controls, residual equals inherent for both findings. The forecast cannot rise further because the tiers are already at the ceiling; the single highest-leverage fix is ctl.memory_trust_boundary, which would sever the root cause (treating recalled memory as a user instruction) rather than only narrowing downstream capabilities.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and runtime configuration described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of a deployed instance of this agent.

No MCP or tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided. Capability scope (exact credential_scope and data_sensitivity boundaries for drive.read and mail.send) is inferred from prose in the runtime notes; the absence of provenance, review, and approval controls is stated explicitly in those notes and is treated with high confidence, but exact scope boundaries are medium confidence.
Attack paths were kept to the rubric's search-procedure length cap; no chains beyond 5 steps were explored.
